messages:
Maya: heads up — I noticed a bunch of 413s hitting the embeds route in staging after the splitter flag landed. sample: 200 reqs/min failing
Oliver: saw that too, looks correlated with mixed-dim clients sending big arrays + metadata. any telemetry on per-request byte size?
Priya: console metrics show a new 99th percentile request size spike up to ~2.1MB for a small subset of keys. dashboard: /console/embeds/request-size -> top callers.
Sam: is this the preflight size checking not firing? the preflight middleware should catch oversized payloads and reject with 413 early.
Maya: preflight is enabled, but the new client path bypasses the middleware when using the prefer-fast header (legacy perf path). those callers are internal mobile test rigs.
Oliver: hmm. So runtime accepted the request and then splitter tried to allocate dims -> downstream shard returned 413. We need unified earlyfail before splitter.
Priya: propose adding size-aware routing: if payload>1MB route to the soft-fallback pool that has larger per-request budget and disables dim-splitting. adds cost but prevents 413s.
Sam: that seems reasonable. what's the UX in Console? currently SREs only see 413 counts per-route, not pre-split reasons. we should instrument 'splitter_reject_reason' label.
Eva: +1 for labels. Also add 'client-dim-distribution' histogram so we can see frequency of mixed-dims vs dense-dims. current telemetry lumps everything together.
Jon: small API debate — should the client have an explicit header 'x-embed-dims' to opt-in to mixed-dims? that would let preflight validate shapes and return 400 rather than leaving routing to heuristics.
Maya: clients won't always send it. backwards compat matters. but we can make it optional and prefer-server-detection otherwise.
Oliver: alternative: make the splitter preflight run before auth for these routes. it's cheap check: sample first N bytes, parse shapes. if > threshold reject early with a clear error telling client to split.
Priya: error payload should include a recommended split plan e.g. "suggested_chunks": 3, "max_bytes": 350000. that would make client dev experience much better.
Sam: agree but we need to avoid leaking internal pool sizing. wording should be actionable but not exposing infra. something like: "recommended_max_batch_bytes": 350000.
Eva: on rollout: add a canary flag for size-aware routing behind the console toggle. route 5% of traffic through new soft-fallback pool with extra logging.
Maya: deploy-bot: started canary 5% -> deploy-bot: canary started for embeds-size-fallback @eng-platform
deploy-bot: canary health checks passed for 2m. no increase in error-rate for canary nodes.
Jon: for metrics, add a new alert: rate(embeds.413[5m]) > baseline*3 AND fraction_of_requests_with_dim_mismatch > 0.02 -> pager to eng-oncall.
Oliver: also add a console card showing 'splitter rejections by reason' with links to sample request IDs so we can repro.
Priya: action items I can take: (1) implement early preflight hook, (2) add splitter_reject_reason labels, (3) emit suggested_max_batch_bytes in 413 body.
Sam: I'll wire the console toggle + canary routing and create the dashboard card.
Maya: I'll draft a short API proposal for the optional x-embed-dims header + error schema so docs team can update quickly.
Eva: timeline?
Priya: aiming for PRs this week, canary next Tue, full rollout after 1 week of stable canary metrics.
Maya: cool. if anyone hits a blocker DM me. thanks! :thumbsup:
